description: Generates a chord progression by walking Bartók's axis system, with a polyphonic chord, a bass note, the notes of the current mode, a gate and a trigger

params.text: Scales the voltage at the bass CV input before it multiplies the bass knob
Scales the voltage at the voicing CV input before it multiplies the voicing knob
Scales the voltage at the chord CV input before it multiplies the chord knob
Scales the voltage at the steps CV input before it multiplies the steps knob
Chooses which note of the chord is taken as the bass: ROOT, 1ST INV or 2ND INV
Chooses the voicing: DEFAULT, OPEN, ROOTLESS or THREE NOTES
Sets how many notes the chord holds, three to seven, which has an effect only under the DEFAULT voicing
Sets how many clock pulses pass before the progression moves to another chord, two to thirty-six
Returns the progression to the tonic and builds a fresh chord
Starts and stops the progression; the module comes up running
From the tonic, the chance of moving to the dominant; the rest of the chance goes to the subdominant
From the subdominant, the chance of moving to the tonic; the rest of the chance goes to the dominant
From the dominant, the chance of moving to the tonic; the rest of the chance goes to the subdominant
Sets the length of the gate output as a share of the gap between clock pulses, never shorter than 1ms

inputs.text: Multiplies the bass knob by this voltage, scaled by the trimmer beside it
Multiplies the voicing knob by this voltage, scaled by the trimmer beside it, so a cable resting at 0V holds the DEFAULT voicing
Multiplies the chord knob by this voltage, scaled by the trimmer beside it; the result is held between three and seven notes
Multiplies the steps knob by this voltage, scaled by the trimmer beside it; the result is held between two and thirty-six
A rising edge above 2V returns the progression to the tonic and builds a fresh chord
A rising edge above 2V starts the progression, and the next one stops it
Each rising edge above 2V is one pulse of the progression; nothing moves until a clock is patched here
Sets the tonic the axis system is built on, read as a pitch; with nothing patched here the tonic is C4

outputs.text: The lowest note of the chord, on its own, an octave below the chord output
Every note of the current mode, one per channel
The chord, one note per channel, with the bass note left out
10V for the share of the clock interval the gate length knob sets, restarted on each clock pulse
A 1ms pulse at 10V on each clock pulse

notes: nothing happens until a clock is patched to the clock input; the module returns early on every sample while that jack is empty
the three circles across the middle of the panel light to show which of the tonic, subdominant and dominant axes the progression is on
menu: Mode transition: Gentle, Rude — Gentle moves between modes in order of brightness, from Lydian down to Locrian, and Rude moves at random
